title: Hairpin lace cowl
subtitle: A joined-loop cowl worked in DK weight on a hairpin lace frame.
excerpt: One hairpin lace strip joined into a tube makes a quick loopy cowl. The loops curl softly around the neck for a textured, lightweight finish in DK weight.
sourceNotes: Hairpin lace cowls made from a single joined strip are a documented quick-project format in modern crochet pattern books. This frame width, loop count, and join method are original to Homemade.

glossaryTerms.definition: A crochet technique where yarn is looped around a U-shaped metal frame while a central chain is worked with a hook, producing a strip of looped fabric on each side.
Joining the two short ends of a hairpin lace strip together to form a continuous loop or tube, used to make cowls and cuffs.

crochet.gaugeText: 14 loops per 10 cm of strip length on a 7 cm wide frame in DK weight.
crochet.finishedSizeText: Cowl approximately 56 cm circumference x 25 cm tall, laid flat.

Set the frame to 7 cm. Work in the standard hairpin lace method with 1 double crochet per rotation. Work until the strip has 78 loops per side (approximately 56 cm). This length, when joined end to end, forms the cowl circumference.

Remove the strip from the frame. Bring the two short ends together with the right side facing out. Join the end loops from each short end by working 1 slip stitch through one loop from each end alternately, using the crochet hook. This forms the tube join. Work along all loops at both ends to close the seam evenly.
Weave in all ends with your tapestry needle through the central spine. The outer loops on both edges sit free. Ease the cowl into shape by hand; no blocking is needed for DK weight.
